topics.topic: Animals and Plants in Our Homes

easy.question: Which of the following is an uninvited guest that appears in our homes on its own?
easy.explanation: Lizards find their way into our homes on their own. Dogs, cats, and parrots are pets we invite home.

easy.question: We should ______ hurt any animal, even the ones that annoy us.
easy.explanation: We should never hurt animals. Most animals will not harm us unless they feel scared or trapped.

easy.question: Name two animals we keep at home as pets.
easy.answer: Dogs and cats are common animals we keep at home as pets.
easy.explanation: People keep dogs, cats, parrots, and fish as pets. They bring us joy and companionship.

easy.question: Which plant is found in almost every Indian home and is used in prayers?
easy.explanation: Tulsi (Holy Basil) is found in most Indian homes. It is used in prayers and has medicinal value.

easy.question: Which uninvited creature spins webs in the corners of our homes?
easy.explanation: Spiders spin webs in corners to catch flies and mosquitoes. They are helpful but uninvited guests.

medium.question: Name three uninvited creatures that visit our homes. Why should we not hurt them?
medium.answer: Chhipkali (lizards), cheetiyan (ants), and makdi (spiders) are uninvited visitors. We should not hurt them because they are harmless and actually help us -- lizards eat mosquitoes, spiders catch flies, and ants clean up crumbs.
medium.explanation: Many creatures enter our homes looking for warmth and food. They play useful roles and deserve our kindness.

medium.question: Which animals are kept at home for their milk?
medium.explanation: Cows and goats are kept at home for their fresh milk.

hard.question: Why should we be kind to all animals, including the ones we do not like? Explain with examples.
hard.answer: We should be kind to all animals because every creature plays an important role in nature. Chhipkali (lizards) eat mosquitoes that could bite us and spread diseases. Makdi (spiders) catch harmful flies in their webs. Even ants help by cleaning up leftover food crumbs. Most animals do not want to hurt us -- they only react when they feel scared or trapped. Instead of killing them, we can gently guide them outside. Being kind to all living things is part of living in harmony with nature.
hard.explanation: Every creature, even the ones we find annoying, has a role in nature. Kindness towards all animals is essential for a balanced world.

topics.topic: How Plants and Animals Help Each Other

easy.question: How do gilhariyan (squirrels) accidentally plant new trees?
options: They bury nuts and forget where they hid them
easy.answer: They bury nuts and forget where they hid them
easy.explanation: Squirrels bury nuts in the soil to eat later, but forget many of them. Those forgotten nuts sprout into new trees!

easy.question: Madhumakkhiyan (honeybees) and titliyan (butterflies) carry ______ from one flower to another, helping plants make fruits.
easy.explanation: Bees and butterflies carry pollen between flowers. This process, called pollination, helps plants produce fruits and seeds.

easy.question: What is seed dispersal?
easy.answer: Seed dispersal is when animals like monkeys and birds eat fruits, carry the seeds far from the parent tree, and drop them in new places. New plants grow from those scattered seeds.
easy.explanation: Animals spread seeds to new locations, allowing plants to grow in different areas. This natural process is called seed dispersal.

easy.question: What do keenchue (earthworms) do that helps plants grow?
options: They make the soil fertile through their droppings
easy.answer: They make the soil fertile through their droppings
easy.explanation: Earthworms burrow through soil and their droppings make it fertile (rich and healthy), helping plants grow stronger.

medium.question: Name three important things that plants give us.
medium.answer: Plants give us food (fruits and vegetables), fresh air (oxygen) to breathe, and medicine (like from neem, tulsi, and haldi).
medium.explanation: Plants provide food, shade, wood, medicine, fibre for clothes, and the fresh oxygen we breathe.

medium.question: How do bandar (monkeys) help plants?
options: They eat fruits and drop seeds far away, helping new plants grow
medium.answer: They eat fruits and drop seeds far away, helping new plants grow
medium.explanation: Monkeys eat fruits and toss seeds far from the parent tree. New plants grow from those scattered seeds.

medium.question: Cotton from plants is used to make ______.
medium.explanation: Cotton is a natural fibre from plants. It is spun into thread and woven into the clothes we wear.

hard.question: Explain how plants, animals, and people all depend on each other. Give at least three examples.
hard.answer: Plants, animals, and people form a circle of giving and receiving. Plants give animals food (fruits, leaves, nectar) and shelter (nests in branches, hollows in trunks). Animals help plants by spreading seeds to new places and keeping soil fertile through their droppings. People help plants by watering them, planting new trees, and protecting forests. People help animals by giving them food, water, and shelter. In return, animals give people milk, eggs, honey, and wool. For example, bees pollinate mango flowers so we get mangoes. Squirrels accidentally plant thousands of trees. Cows eat grass and give us fresh milk every day.
hard.explanation: Plants, animals, and people are all connected in a beautiful circle. This is what living in harmony means.

hard.question: How can you make a plant your friend? Why is having a plant friend a good idea?
hard.answer: To make a plant friend, choose a tree, shrub, or pot plant near your home or school. Give it a name, water it regularly, and pull out weeds around it. Watch it closely as its leaves, buds, flowers, and fruits change with the seasons. You can sit near your plant when you feel happy, sad, or worried. Having a plant friend is a good idea because it teaches you to care for nature and be responsible. Spending time near plants makes you feel calm and peaceful. It also helps the environment because a well-cared-for plant gives clean air and shade.
hard.explanation: Adopting a plant friend connects you to nature, teaches responsibility, and brings a sense of peace and happiness.

topics.topic: The Grey Wagtails and Caring for Nature

easy.question: What kind of food do ants rush to first?
easy.explanation: Ants almost always rush to sweet things first! If you put sugar near an ant trail, they will come quickly.

easy.question: The Grey Wagtail bird is called Vaalatti Kuruvi in ______.
easy.explanation: The Grey Wagtail is known as Vaalatti Kuruvi in Tamil. It visits the hill town of Valparai every winter.

easy.question: Why are Grey Wagtails called 'Wagtails'?
easy.answer: They are called Wagtails because they are always bobbing their tails up and down, like a happy little wave.
easy.explanation: Grey Wagtails constantly wag their tails, which is how they got their name.

easy.question: In which hill town of Tamil Nadu do children celebrate when Grey Wagtails arrive?
easy.explanation: In Valparai, children and teachers celebrate the arrival of Grey Wagtails by putting up welcome posters and sharing sweets.

medium.question: How do the people of Valparai welcome the Grey Wagtails?
medium.answer: When the first Grey Wagtail arrives in Valparai, schoolchildren and teachers celebrate by putting up colourful welcome posters and handing out mithai (sweets) to everyone.
medium.explanation: The Grey Wagtails fly from cold mountains to warmer Valparai during winter, and the town celebrates their arrival.

medium.question: Why do Grey Wagtails fly to Valparai?
options: To escape the chilly winter cold in the mountains
medium.answer: To escape the chilly winter cold in the mountains
medium.explanation: During chilly winter months, Grey Wagtails fly from the cold mountains to warmer towns like Valparai.

hard.question: What does 'living in harmony' mean? How can we live in harmony with plants and animals?
hard.answer: Living in harmony means understanding that plants, animals, and people are all connected and need each other. We can live in harmony by planting trees and watering them regularly, being kind to all animals including uninvited ones in our homes, keeping water out for birds in summer, not cutting trees unnecessarily, and respecting every form of life. We can adopt a plant friend and care for it. We can celebrate nature like the children of Valparai celebrate the Grey Wagtails. When we take care of nature, nature takes care of us by giving food, clean air, medicine, and a beautiful world to live in.
hard.explanation: Living in harmony means treating all living things with respect and understanding that we are all part of the same circle of life.
